verdict.rationale: PayPal's agent toolkit documents first-party create_refund and get_refund tools for refunding a captured payment, either the full amount or a specified amount, and for retrieving refund status, so refunds can be initiated and tracked programmatically on the PayPal REST rails. Coverage is incomplete because the docs never connect these tools to orders placed through the agentic channels, and the ACP/UCP paths settle through Braintree single-use tokens with no documented refund path. Store Sync orders are also routed into the merchant's own order management system. Missing for 10: documented refund handling for Braintree-processed ACP/UCP agent orders, refund-specific webhook event types for asynchronous tracking, and independent or hands-on corroboration of refunds on agent-placed orders.

support.subject: As a developer, refunds on agent-placed orders can be initiated and tracked programmatically

citations.quote: Post-purchase operations are first-class agent tools: refunds via create_refund / get_refund (a "refund for a captured payment", where "If not specified, a refund is for the full amount of the purchase")
the SDK covering orders, invoices, subscriptions, tracking, disputes, refunds, and transactions
